pool.text: The Dutch East India Company established a trade post in Palembang.
The Grand Mosque of Palembang was built under the reign of Sultan Mahmud Badaruddin I Jaya Wikrama.
Palembang was incorporated into the Dutch East Indies after the abolition of the Palembang Sultanate.
Dulmuluk was adapted into a local theatrical performance by Palembangnese.
The Post and Telegraph Office opened its doors in Palembang.
Javasche Bank was established in Palembang.
The town hall with its remarkable water tower was built.
The first plane landed at Palembang airport in Talang Betutu.
USAAF B-29 bombers flying from India raided the Palembang refineries.
Palembang was occupied by the Dutch after an urban battle with Republicans.
Cinde Market was built with its unique mushroom pillars.
Ampera Bridge was completed and officially opened for public.
Indonesia government expanded Palembang's administrative area as far as 12 kilometers from the city center.
Musi II Bridge was built crossing Musi River.
President Susilo Bambang Yudhoyono declared Palembang a Water Tourism City.
Palembang's first flyover was completed at Simpang Polda.
Palembang launched its bus transit system, Transmusi.
Palembang replaced Riau province capital Pekanbaru as host city of the Islamic Solidarity Games.
The central government began upgrading Palembang's transportation with the construction of a light rail transit system.
South Sumatra is the largest producer of rubber, with over 850,000 tons exported from Palembang.
